title: Grateful Dead Live at Nassau Coliseum on 1982-04-11
lineage: (9th row - center) Senn 421's > Sony TC D5 > Playback on Nak Dragon > Sony R700 DAT deck (sbm-on) - used only as A>D converter (44.1khz) > ZA2 > CDR (x1) >EAC >SHN (tracking with CDWAV)

ai_review.summary: A decent audience‑recording of the 4/11/82 show with a few shining moments (Let It Grow, Never Trust A Woman) but a generally uneven performance.
ai_review.review: The tape captures a mixed night – the first set starts shaky and suffers from occasional lyrical flubs, while the second half offers some sparkle, especially on Let It Grow and the post‑space stretch of Never Trust A Woman. The audience‑recorded source is listenable despite bumps and a thin opening, making it worth a spin for fans who enjoy the quirks of this era.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is uneven (average‑to‑good) while the recording is generally listenable and decent; combined weighting yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listenably clear for an audience tape (9th row‑center), but the opening of both sets has equipment bumps, muffled lyrics and occasional drop‑outs.

poor_songs: Good Lovin' (band almost quits, Brent leaves stage)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens rough with lyrical slips and a shaky start, but recovers toward the end; second set sparkles early then loses momentum after Good Lovin'.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note Jerry’s enjoyable vibe, hot licks, strong vocal on Candyman and extra‑something solos to cover lyrical slips.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent is highlighted – he quits the stage during Good Lovin', adds scat singing on Rooster (Around) and delivers a high organ note that “lights ears on fire.”
